questions.text: You drop a heavy yam and a light pebble from the same height at the exact same time. What happens?

options.text: The heavy yam hits the ground first because it has more weight.
The light pebble hits the ground first because it faces less air resistance.
They both hit the ground at the exact same time.
The yam falls faster at first, then the pebble catches up.

questions.explanation: Galileo proved that gravity accelerates all objects at the exact same rate (9.8 m/s²), regardless of their mass. Air resistance can slow lighter, flatter objects down (like a feather), but for dense objects like a yam and a pebble, the effect of air is negligible. Thus, they hit the ground simultaneously.

questions.text: A boy kicks a football high into the air. While the ball is flying in the air (and ignoring wind), what forces are pushing it FORWARD?

options.text: The force of the kick stays with the ball and keeps pushing it.
There is no forward force pushing it; it moves forward because of inertia (its starting motion).
Gravity pushes it forward in an arc.
The air pushes it forward from behind.

questions.explanation: This tests a classic misconception known as "impetus theory". Once the ball leaves the foot, the kick is over; there is no longer any forward force acting on it. It continues to move forward purely because of inertia (Newton's First Law). The only force acting on it in flight is gravity pulling it downward.

questions.text: A fast-moving Danfo bus collides with a small stationary bicycle. During the crash, which experiences a greater impact force?

options.text: The Danfo bus exerts a much larger force on the bicycle.
The bicycle exerts a larger force on the Danfo bus.
They both exert the exact same amount of force on each other.
The Danfo bus absorbs all the force since it is heavier.

questions.explanation: According to Newton's Third Law, every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The force the bus exerts on the bicycle is exactly equal in magnitude to the force the bicycle exerts on the bus. The reason the bicycle is destroyed while the bus is barely dented is because the bicycle has much less mass, so the same force causes a much greater acceleration (damage) on it (F = ma).

readingTasks.subject: Chemistry
readingTasks.title: How Electrons Inhabit Energy Shells
readingTasks.content:
Electrons are not tiny planets orbiting a sun in neat flat circles. In modern chemistry, electrons occupy three-dimensional regions of probability called orbitals.

The principal energy levels (n = 1, 2, 3...) tell you the main distance from the nucleus. Within each level, there are subshells: s, p, d, and f.

• The 's' subshell has 1 orbital and holds a maximum of 2 electrons.
• The 'p' subshell has 3 orbitals and holds a maximum of 6 electrons.
• The 'd' subshell has 5 orbitals and holds a maximum of 10 electrons.

Remember the Aufbau principle: electrons always fill lower energy levels before moving to higher ones.

recallQuestion.questionText: What is the maximum number of electrons that can fit into any p subshell?

options.text: 2 electrons
6 electrons
10 electrons
14 electrons

recallQuestion.explanation: A p subshell contains 3 orbitals. Each orbital holds a maximum of 2 electrons, for a total of 3 × 2 = 6 electrons.

readingTasks.subject: Mathematics
readingTasks.title: Why Inverse Operations Work in Algebra
readingTasks.content:
Solving an algebraic equation is like unwrapping a package in reverse order.

If you take a number x, multiply it by 2, and add 5 to get 11:
1. The last thing done to x was adding 5.
2. To unwrap it, first subtract 5 from both sides: 2x = 6.
3. The remaining operation on x is multiplication by 2. To unwrap it, divide both sides by 2: x = 3.

Always undo addition and subtraction before undoing multiplication and division.

recallQuestion.questionText: In the equation 3x + 7 = 19, which operation should you perform first on both sides?

options.text: Divide both sides by 3
Subtract 7 from both sides
Multiply both sides by 19
Add 7 to both sides

recallQuestion.explanation: Always undo the constant term added or subtracted first to isolate the variable term.

readingTasks.subject: Chemistry
readingTasks.title: How Scientific Models Work: From Intuition to Evidence
readingTasks.content:
Welcome to Science Transition Academy. When returning to science after months or years, the most critical shift is moving away from memorising formulas without meaning.

Science is not a collection of disconnected facts to be memorized for a single test. It is an interlocking web of mental models that explain why things happen.

• In Physics, we observe motion and ask: what forces are acting, and why?
• In Chemistry, we observe substances and ask: how are the electrons and atoms arranged?
• In Biology, we observe life and ask: how do cells and systems maintain energy and balance?

Take your time with each question. If you make a mistake, read the full explanation to repair the mental model.

recallQuestion.questionText: What is the most effective way to rebuild science knowledge according to the Academy model?

options.text: Cramming exam past questions without explanations
Rebuilding core mental models and understanding the reasoning underneath
Memorizing formulas without checking relationships
Skipping mathematics when studying chemistry and physics

recallQuestion.explanation: True mastery requires repairing the foundational concepts and relationships underneath the formulas.
